units.text: We'll match each service to its release job. CodePipeline coordinates stages and approvals. CodeBuild builds and tests the artifact. CodeDeploy changes an application deployment, while CodeArtifact stores supported packages. Don't ask the service that stores a package to decide whether the application is healthy.

Compare the blast radius and capacity. Rolling updates replace batches, but capacity can shrink during the rollout. Canary exposes a small traffic share first. Blue-green prepares another environment and can make a switch back easier while the old environment is available. Check what the target supports.
The build gate checks the tests and scan evidence for this artifact. If those checks fail, stop promotion. Keep the digest so the same candidate can be reviewed and deployed.

The approval gate checks whether the identified candidate is allowed to proceed. A rejection or timeout stops deployment on this path. Approval does not substitute for tests and doesn't validate a different digest.
Once the canary is running, watch errors and latency. If the configured alarm triggers the rollback, confirm traffic returned to the prior version.
One thing stays separate: a traffic rollback doesn't undo data writes already made. Verify and recover those effects separately.
